en:
I mean, since this is where
people with mechanical bodies
live on a planet that's
supposed to be uninhabited,
I was expecting some amazing\narchitecture, like when we saw\nValka's ship on Daftes...

How should I put it... it feels
exactly like a roadside shack.
Rubarika had plenty of houses
like this.
This is a paper book... no, a\nmagazine.
A mag-a-zine?

It's a composite publication. A type of
book where articles and photos from
many different people are published
based on a specific theme.
Judging by the cover, I believe\nthis one is a magazine themed\naround science and technology.
What's that thing shooting fire\nand flying behind the old guy's\nface?
...This is strange. Why... why\nwould a magazine like that be\nin a place like this?
...I can't believe it... everything\nis exactly as the records\ndescribed...
Mista Kevin, let me confirm.\nMista is...
No, could it be that Planet\nRaza is...

If my foster father had
survived like I did, I'm sure he
would have wanted to meet
you, Valka S90.
...Then, it really is true.
Yes. It is as you suspect.
I don't suspect a damn thing...\nWhat's going on?

Why have Valka, Coro, and the
Captain been freaking out for a
while now? ...Don't tell me you
guys actually know Kevin.
It's not exactly that we are\n"acquaintances."
But... Mista Kevin's foster\nfather and my father... were\nlikely acquainted.
Huh...?
I see. So you were his\ndaughter.

What do you mean? Are you saying
your father came all the way to the
Azurite system on some mission for the
Hardier Warrior of Morphus?
To be precise, Valka's father\nonce set foot on Planet Raza.
However, he never visited the\nAzurite system.
This makes no sense.
When Valka's father... Bacchus\nD-79, met my father-in-law,\nKlaus Barktain,

Planet Raza was located in a place
called the Solar System, at the far
edge of a galaxy much further than the
Azurite system.
The Solar System... Captain...\nCoro, that means...

Back when it was in the Solar
System... the people living on
Planet Raza called their world
this.
... "Earth."
T-that can't be right! Raza\nbeing Earth... that's impossible!
...My father used to call that\nplanet <font color=yellow>Another Earth</font>.
Another Earth? "Another\nland"...? What does that mean?

...Mista Heath, you were able to
understand the meaning of
that phrase, based on the
language of Earth, immediately.
This fact alone leaves no room\nfor doubt that Raza is Another\nEarth.
To us, it means "Another\nEarth"... but...

Exactly. Another Earth is a
"second Earth" that shouldn't
exist. An Earth that existed in
another dimension.
And that Earth... shortly after\nmy father and his companions\narrived...
...was supposed to have\nvanished completely from the\nuniverse.
Oh? Vanished.
Mista Heath. You mentioned\nthis before.

That before Gems were
discovered on Raza, starships
were powered by a different
energy source.
Yeah.
Was that energy source\n<font color=yellow>Exalithium crystals</font>?
! How do you... Did your old\nman tell you that too?
Yes. It is a name my father and\nhis companions can never\nforget.

Because... the direct cause of
Another Earth's disappearance
from the solar system was
those Exalithium crystals.
What?

When my father first arrived on
Another Earth, it was still in the early
stages of space exploration. Resources
were scarce worldwide, and scientific
progress was sluggish.

But one day, Exalithium
crystals―an innovative energy
source from an advanced
civilization―were brought there.

And then... a scientist,
captivated by them, attempted
to control the crystals using an
unfinished antimatter reactor...
He failed.
Anti-matter? What's that?
...To put it in terms you'd\nunderstand,

It's a dangerous energy source.
A piece the size of a pinky nail
could wipe Rubarika off the
map without leaving a trace.
A bit oversimplified, but not\nwrong.

With Exalithium crystals, no matter how
small the fragment, blowing up a whole
planet is a breeze once you trigger
annihilation.
...And the name of the\nantimatter reactor used at\nthat time was...
...Kevin.
You are well-informed.

I've heard that your father...
and your comrades... regretted
it from the bottom of their
hearts.
It was not the fault of your\nfather and the others, Valka.

The responsibility lies entirely with my
stepmother, who could not discipline
herself, and my stepfather, who failed
to stop her.
Your stepmother's name was...\n<font color=yellow>Mira Baktain</font>, was it not?

...It is a complete coincidence
that my name is "Kevin." My
biological parents gave me this
name.
And then... shortly after the\nday the world changed... that\nday of tragedy...
I met my foster parents.
Bacchus D-79, Edge Maverick,\nReimi Saionji,
Phase Cipher Beres, Rimuru\nRemuri Fai,
and Merikuru Shamlot.
My foster father always said\nthey were the most radiant\npeople in this world.

When they arrived, "our Earth"
in the year 1957 AD was on
the brink of a global energy
crisis.

In the midst of that, my foster
mother rashly reached out for
an unknown energy brought
from "their Earth."

My father claimed to have
confirmed the complete
annihilation of the other... no,
your Earth.
How could Mrs. Mira and\nDoctor Klaus have survived?
...Earth had not been\nannihilated. It had been warped\nto the Azurite system.
Warped...?
As for why that happened...\neven now, I do not know for\ncertain.

<font color=blue>Kevin</font> When Edge Maverick's
party appeared, my foster
mother obtained one prisoner
and an Exalithium crystal.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> A prisoner... Reimi Saionji,\nthen.

<font color=blue>Kevin</font> Yes. At first, my stepmother
focused her efforts on the medical
study of Reimi Saionji, as she was an
"alien."

...However, once she obtained
the Exalithium crystal, she
prioritized the completion of
the antimatter reactor,
...and she failed to control it.
The antimatter reactor went\ncritical, and Earth was swept\nup in a vortex of energy.
My stepmother and stepfather\nprepared themselves for death.
...But at the final moment, they\nboth saw something.
<font color=blue>Kevin</font> They saw light stretching\nfrom the antimatter reactor\nout into space.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> Stretching into space?

<font color=blue>Kevin</font> Yes. ...As for why Earth
warped to the Azurite system,
my stepfather once offered an
analysis of sorts.

Exalithium crystals are substances that
connect space to space, and are
essential for activating a subspace
Warp Drive.

And at that time, there was
another powerful Exalithium
crystal present, aside from the
one built into the reactor.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> ...Merikuru Shamlot's\npendant...

<font color=blue>Kevin</font> Yes. Those two
Exalithium crystals reacted
with one another, creating a
spatial rift.

Earth was swallowed by that
rift... and the entire planet was
warped to another star
system.

That was my stepfather's
analysis, though it was based
largely on inference and wishful
thinking.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> I can't believe it... If\nthat's true, it can only be\ndescribed as a miracle...

<font color=blue>Welch</font> I don't really get it, but is it like
when Baschen sent us flying to Daftes,
except the whole planet flew far away
into the sky?
I'm starting to get confused\nagain.

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> It's like if all of Daftine
moved to the Azurite system. If
that happened, the whole
planet would be in total chaos.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Still, to have moved
into the habitable zone of
another star system is an
unbelievable stroke of luck.
Are the environments of the\nAzurite system and the Solar\nSystem really that similar?
<font color=blue>Kevin</font> Of course, many\nproblems arose.

Changes to the planetary environment
due to the shift in the axial tilt,
changes in the nature of the solar wind,
and so on...

While the star itself survived, many fell victim to
the great cataclysm or failed to adapt to the
changing environment. The population
plummeted to a tenth of its former size, and
civilization regressed significantly.
That happened... approximately\n670 years ago.

Still, it is hard to believe that you could
overcome a disaster that caused such
a regression and rebuild your
civilization to the point of waging
interstellar war once more.

The fact that Milla and Klaus's research
facility remained intact, despite being
the source of that great cataclysm, is
what prevented the total collapse of
our civilization.

Furthermore, that facility
contained the Hint on how to
"reincarnate Earthlings as
Raza,"
...the hints for "adapting them\nto a new environment" were\nleft behind.

Over a long period of time, this
was gradually implemented
across all of humanity on
Earth.
Adapt to the environment...\nSurely you don't mean...

Yes. Exactly. The secret hidden
within the body of Reimi
Saionji, whom my foster
mother... Milla captured...

A mysterious gene that allows
the physical body to adapt to
any environment, as long as it
is within a habitable zone.
I am of the first generation\nentrusted with those "genes."
A survivor of the children\nraised in Milla's research\nfacility.

Milla and Klaus gave a name to
those of us who survived the
Great Catastrophe as the new
humans of Earth.
The children of luck. The\n<font color=yellow>Fortune Babies</font>.

This building where I reside in Lazuli is
a recreation of the hut where my
father-in-law used to converse with
Bacchus D-79 and the others.

I thought that by staying here, I might
be able to see something regarding the
future of the stars... and of this Azurite
system.
...It is hard to believe, but much\nof this aligns with the stories I\nheard from my father...
If that is the case, then what\nMista Kevin says is true,
And the planet Raza... is\nanother Earth that came from\nanother dimension.
Hey, can I ask something?

Assuming what Valka said is
true... does that mean you've
been alive for at least 600
years?
Well, if you can call existing in\nthis state "living."
I think you're alive, so that's\ngood enough for me.
In that case, there's something\nI want to know.
...Yes, what is it?
This "Kevin" who started the\nStardust Bazaar... was that\nyou?
There is no point in hiding it.\nThat is correct.

...Do you ever think that the
independence of the Stardust Bazaar
was, in the end, a distant cause of the
interstellar war between Raza and
Ober?

I do. Though I never imagined a
war of this scale would break
out, nor that it would drag on
for so long.
...I'll ask you this. Knowing that,\nwhy did you do it?

To prevent the calamity
brought about by my
stepmother from happening
again.
What?

Whether it be Exalithium crystals or
Gems, it took a terrifying amount of
time and sacrifice before they could be
stably controlled as they are now.

The most extreme example of
this, as I mentioned, was the
risk of an entire planet
vanishing.

...If the Bazaar were to fall into
the hands of either planet now,
a similar tragedy would surely
occur. I must prevent that.
...I'm going to be blunt here.
It was your old lady who\nscrewed up,

and isn't it a bit much to pin
that on the general lack of
awareness among all of
humanity?

It is also true that there are
countless others capable of
making the same mistakes my
stepmother did.

My stepmother confused her own
misfortunes with the noble cause of
saving the world, eventually resorting to
inhumane experiments and triggering
the Great Calamity.
Whatever humans are capable\nof doing, there is a possibility it\nwill happen again.

Therefore, it is not unnatural
for those who know the truth
to fear it and seek measures
to prevent its recurrence.
But still...!
Furthermore, I am not speaking\nwithout evidence.
Heath, you likely only know\nthat the Gem hunters of\nSatellite Rigas, myself included,
discovered a new vein and\nestablished the Stardust\nBazaar.
In that case, let me ask you\nthis:

Why do you think someone like
me, who could have become
the supreme authority of the
Stardust Bazaar,
is living a life of seclusion on a\nplanet like this?
Exactly. Long before we ever\nfound the asteroid belt of the\nStardust Bazaar,

Long before the asteroid belt of the
Stardust Bazaar was ever discovered, I
found *it* here on Lazuli, back when no
one paid this planet any mind.

That stone gate, which
possesses a power beyond
human understanding or
imagination.
...The Urza System...
I call that stone gate the <font color=yellow>Lazuli\nStone</font>.

No matter what happens, it is
something that must never fall
into the hands of Raza or
Ober.
You sound as if you know\nsomething specific regarding\nthat gate.
...I can say no more than that.
It is not a conversation I should\nbe having within earshot of a\nRaza soldier,
And if you'll pardon my bluntness, there\nis no guarantee that you all wouldn't\nabuse the truth once you learned it.
Huh?! You can't be serious\nafter we've come all this way!

We don't even know why the
planetary governments are
fighting over this place! If you
know something, just tell us!
I cannot.

Besides, even if the current Raza and
Ober people heard what I've said, it
would only cause some unrest and lead
them to reconsider their roots.
But the Lazuli Stone is\ndifferent. That... can clearly\nchange the future.
Master Mastima: ...Are you\nreferring to the power of Event\nExtraction?
Master Mastima?
Event Extraction? What are\nyou talking about?

Master Mastima: As I said
before, projecting images of
the past is merely a secondary
effect of that stone gate.
Master Mastima: It was\ncreated for a different\npurpose.
Wait! Why would you do such a\nthing...?!

There are some circumstances.
I've simply looked over the
research materials regarding
that gate.

The Lazuli Stone... the primary
function of the Urza System is
the "Extraction of Specific
Temporal Events."
What does that mean?
Exactly what it sounds like.

I've heard it's a technology that
can summon something from a
projected image of the past
into this very moment.
It "summons objects or people\nacross time."
That's just like...!
Yes. Does it remind you of\nsomething?
Like Evelysse's... summons?

I've heard that as long as the
conditions are met, the Urza
System can summon a
considerable amount of mass.
Who knows? It might even be\npossible to summon an entire\nplanet.
...What are you talking about?\nSuch an absurd power is surely\nimpossible.
...A space-time warp shield...
Hm?
The mass of an entire planet\ncrossing through time...

The Galactic Federation has
already confirmed that
phenomenon as a scientific
fact.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> The technology to use a powerful
gravitational field to phase-shift space-time and
interfere with the flow of time within a closed
space already existed in Energy Nede 700
million years ago.

<font color=blue>Heath</font> Hey, all this complicated
talk is coming at me one after
another. I'm starting to lose
track here.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> To put it simply, we have already
confirmed instances where "a lost star
was extracted from a past timeline and
revived."

<font color=blue>Heath</font> ...Everything you guys
talk about is on such a
massive scale that I just don't
get it.

Summoning a whole planet
from the past? How... and why
on earth would anyone do such
a thing...?
<font color=blue>Kevin</font> ...

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> In this vast universe, there
were fools driven so far to the edge
that they had to seriously consider
such madness.

Though, I never heard that this
so-called space-time warp shield was
ever completed before I was cast out
of paradise.

The Captain, Coro, and Valka
S90 are likely more
knowledgeable about these
matters.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Indeed. Energy Nede. Energy
Nede are fragments of the planet Nede.
They vanished from the universe as if
fleeing from their own sins.

On the other hand, Vandione, who
refused to be bound by the prisons of
the universe, set out to protect a new
cosmic order.

And... there was also a faction
that researched and applied
the Urza System, plotting the
revival of the planet Nede.
Well, as you know, it seems\nthey weren't successful.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> Why did it fail?
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Simply put, they\nlacked the energy.

Pulling out a mass as enormous and
complex as an entire planet is a
completely different story from pulling
out a single human.
<font color=blue>Henri</font> Even for a single human,\nthat's generally quite a feat.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> The cause of failure for those who
might be called the Nede Revivalists was that
they couldn't accumulate enough energy or
prepare a caster capable of controlling it in
time.
<font color=blue>Henri</font> Then, conversely, if they\nhad succeeded...
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> There would be one\nmore star in this universe that\nshouldn't exist right now.

Well, according to Coro, there are
cases where stars that should have
vanished were restored, separate from
Planet Nede.
I'll have to hear more about\nthat in due time.
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> What's important now\nis that the Urza System is here\non Planet Lazuli.

That significantly changes the
meaning behind why Raza and
Ober are fighting over this
planet.
<font color=blue>Heath</font> You're saying both Raza\nand Ober are aware of this\n"Urza System" thing?

<font color=blue>Valka</font> Yeah. In an interstellar war
spanning twenty years, you have to
assume there's a hidden objective that
hasn't been made public.

...Tell me, Mastima. You
mentioned earlier that the Urza
System requires energy to
operate.
In this case, the energy\nsource... is it what I think it is?
From here on, this is nothing\nmore than my speculation.

However, the Evelysse in the
recording possessed a massive
amount of cargo stolen from
Lavarnia.
And there is a man who established the\nStardust Bazaar, which controls the\nprimary resources of the star system.

And the man who established the
Stardust Bazaar to control the
system's primary resources is right
here, keeping watch over that gate.
With all these pieces in place,\nthe answer should be simple,\nwouldn't you say?
If that's the case, then what on\nearth are Raza and Ober\ngathering them for...?
...Gems.
In that case, I am concerned\nabout the Thornite.

The fact that a Thornite is
near a gate with the limited
ability to interfere with
space-time is...
I heard about this from\nEvelysse before.

Givel said that the Thornite's
thorns act as antennas and
needles to repair dimensional
rifts.

So, I think it's trying to repair
the space-time distortion
caused by the gate's power
this time too.
Hmm... so the Thornite appears\nwhenever time is crossed.

Then what about the incident at the
Bazaar? Was the Thornite that
appeared in the Rose family's
warehouse separate from Givel's?
We don't have nearly enough\ninformation right now. Don't get\nahead of yourself.

For now, we have no way off
this planet. Besides, our
primary goal is to get Heath
back to the mothership.

True. Since there is so much
we can't confirm, we should
focus on the goals right in
front of us.

But given the state of the
Overman... all we can do now is
wait for the ship to be
repaired...
Hm? Speaking of which, what\nhappened to the owner of the\nOverman?
I noticed Welch disappeared at\nsome point. No wonder it\nsuddenly got so quiet.
Oh, those two?

They went to repair the ship just now,
taking Euwin along and using the
maintenance machine they borrowed
from Kevin.
Welch said that since I wouldn't\nunderstand anyway, she'd just\ntell me later.
...Poor Euwin, getting dragged\ninto that.
No, I'm thinking of Euwin.

He likely volunteered to keep
an eye on things so Welch
wouldn't break the Overman or
Kevin's machine.
In any case, let us wait for the\nOverman to be repaired.

We've had one trouble after another,
and we've received far too much new
information. Everyone here must be
exhausted, both mentally and
physically.
We should take a short break.
True that. I don't even know\nwhat I'm doing or what I'm\nlistening to anymore.

Kevin. I wish to apologize for intruding
upon your territory so suddenly and for
prying into your affairs in such an
abrupt manner.

That being said, I have a
request. Please, let us rest
until the situation aboard the
Overman improves.
...Yes, that is fine. I also have a\nfew more things I would like to\nask...
Captain. Coro.
If you wouldn't mind, could you\ntell me?
What the "Earth" in this\nuniverse, in this dimension, is\nlike right now...
How's it going? Is the repair\nproceeding smoothly?
Oh. Are you guys done talking\nalready?
Not exactly, but we're taking a\nquick break.

In the end, there were still a lot
of things that didn't quite add
up regarding that gate and the
reason for the war.
Hmm. I see.
So? Euwin, you look exhausted.\nIt doesn't seem like you're just\nhelping with the repairs...
Ah, well, there's just... quite a\nlot of Thornite around here,\nwhew...
You can't be serious! Were you\nfighting the Thornite all by\nyourself!?
I wouldn't say fighting, more\nlike driving them away...
You see, we accidentally broke\na bit of Kevin's big machine.
Right now, a spare machine is\nhandling the capture, but...
It's a spare, so it's wimpy. It\ngets tossed around easily.

It's getting in the way of the
Overman's repairs, too. That's
why I told little Eu to go give
them a hand.
You should have sent someone\nto get him. What if he got\nseriously hurt?

Oh, no, the fighting itself isn't
that hard. Besides the spare
machine, Lavarnia's... thing is
helping out too.
Thing... you mean those wings\non Lavarnia's back?

Right?! Isn't it amazing?! I heard Lover
can make them fly and even perform
simple attacks just by thinking about
it!!
Huh. It is impressive. But why\nare you the one bragging about\nit?
Because I'm going to have\nthem teach me how to make\nsome! Hehehehe.
...Anyway, they seemed to be\nhaving fun, so I just got caught\nup in it.
I wish Mastima's research were\nas heartwarming as you two...

By the way, is there anything I
can do to help? Looking at the
situation, it might be a good
time to switch with Euwin.
...That would be a help. Euwin\nsays that, but his movements\nwere starting to slow down.
Haha...

Of course. Go get some rest.
Since we're capturing it, we
can't beat it up too badly,
right?
...It seems so. Look, it's already\nhere.
Those wings act as eyes, don't\nthey?
Leave it to me. I'll give it a little\ntwist.
...Impressive.

I had the support of your
wings. Otherwise, I might have
accidentally taken out two or
three more.
...Thank you.
I'm sorry. We ended up\ndestroying your ship for our\nown convenience.
...It can't be helped. It was to\nrepay the debt of saving my\nlife.
I don't think it was quite that\ndramatic. Besides, you're a\npretty capable fighter yourself.
...I'm not as accustomed to\ncombat as you and the others,\nKarlyn.
Oh, really?
On our ship, we have a\nmachine called "Lambda."

It has something called an "AI,"
which allows it to judge and
act on its own without anyone
giving it orders.
...And?

But with your mechanical
wings, you're the one making
the judgments and directing
every move, right?

Your support for me and the
capture machines was precise.
That's not something you can
do without combat experience.
...Do you think so?
Hey, Eu! If you're just lounging\naround, give me a hand. Bring\nthat radiator over here.
I'm resting because I need to\nrest! Which one is the\nradiator?
That thing to your left! The one\nthat's all clunky!
What do you mean "clunky\nmachine"... Is this it?!
Yep! Can you attach that to\nthe top part over there?
Where?! How am I supposed to\ndo that?!
Just make it look good!
No way! Lavarnia will get mad\nat me!
...Those two.
Hmm?
...Are Euwin and Welch lovers?
Oh, aren't they basically\nmarried?
What!? They're married!?

Oh, sorry. I didn't mean literally.
I just mean they don't have
that unstable, immature kind of
"lover" relationship.
They've developed a bond\nmore like "family"―something\nthat can't be severed.
...Family.
They accept any absurdity...\nthough it's usually Welch\ncausing it...

And if one of them is about to
go astray... again, probably
Welch... the other would risk
their life to bring them back.

Normally, they understand each other
without saying a word, and they share
everything, from the joyful moments to
the infuriating ones.
If you asked me what that kind\nof relationship is, I couldn't find\na word other than "married."
Just don't tell them I said that.\nThey'll get angry.
...Strange. It's the complete\nopposite of my father and\nmother.
Huh?
...My parents... they ended up\ntogether after a great\nromance.
Is that so?

Succubus are often called a
race that seduces men of
other species, but that's not
exactly right.

We simply unravel the other
person's guard and steal their
Gem power through their
dreams.
Well, I suppose it depends on\nhow you interpret "unraveling"\nsomeone's guard...
...But we are destined to stay\nwith only one person for our\nentire lives.
Until that one person is found,\nwe must absolutely protect\nourselves.
And then... when the time\ncomes, we fall deeply in love.
I see.

Apparently, my mother simply couldn't
unravel my father's heart or peek into
his dreams, and she became desperate
to know what he was thinking.

She chased him for years and
years, until she realized she
couldn't think of anything but
him.
That's why she always told me\nshe wanted me to find\nsomeone like that for myself.
...Wait, could it be?
...Just so we're clear, I'm not\ntalking about Heath.
Oh?
And it's not a case of me being\nshy and actually meaning him,\neither.
My, my...
...Heath is different. It's true we\nwere close back when he was\nwith Rose's family...
But Heath is simple; it's easy\nto see right through him.
He always treats me like a\nchild.

Even now. He thinks I'm just
some pampered princess who
can't do anything without my
father protecting me.
...I see.
...I just wanted to show him\nthat I'm not like that. That's all.
I see... Yeah. I think that's a\ngood goal to have.
...Ms. Karlyn?
It's nothing. I just think you're\ndoing fine as you are.

Sorry for interrupting your
work. Could you keep an eye
on Welch for a little while?
Thanks.
...O-okay...
There! All done! Thanks for the\nhelp. You're always so reliable,\nEuwin!
Yeah, yeah, you're welcome.\nCan I take a break now?
